summary: This Investopedia-style article introduces the oil and gas industry for investors, explaining that it is one of the largest sectors by dollar value, with an estimated $5 trillion in global revenue as of 2022. It describes how hydrocarbons form and are trapped in reservoirs, the three industry segments (upstream, midstream, downstream), and the units used to measure oil and gas production and reserves. It also covers integrated oil companies, leading producing countries, and the three P categories of reserves.
one_line: An investor-oriented introduction to the oil and gas industry's upstream, midstream and downstream segments, hydrocarbon formation, production units and reserve classifications.
key_facts: The oil and gas industry is estimated to generate $5 trillion in global revenue as of 2022.
Hydrocarbons make up crude oil and natural gas and are created by the compression of remains of plants and animals in sedimentary rocks such as sandstone, limestone, and shale.
Oil and gas are less dense than water, so they migrate through porous sedimentary rock toward the earth's surface until trapped beneath less-porous cap rock, forming a reservoir.
Upstream companies, known as E&P (exploration and production) companies, find reservoirs and drill oil and gas wells.
Midstream businesses are focused on transportation, moving extracted raw materials to refineries via shipping, trucking, pipelines, and storage.
Downstream businesses are refineries and gas stations; refineries produce products such as gasoline, jet fuel, heating oil, and asphalt.
One barrel of oil (bbl) is equal to 42 U.S. gallons.
The prefix M indicates 1,000 and MM indicates 1 million, so Mbbl is 1,000 barrels and MMbbl is 1 million barrels.
Mmcf means 1 million cubic feet of gas, Bcf means 1 billion cubic feet, and Tcf means 1 trillion cubic feet.
Natural gas futures on the CME Group are based on 1 million British thermal units (MMBtu), roughly equivalent to 970 cubic feet of gas.
One barrel of oil equivalent (BOE) has the energy equivalent of 6,040 cubic feet of gas, or roughly one bbl to six Mcf.
As of 2022, the United States is the world's largest net producer of crude oil, followed by Saudi Arabia, Russia, Canada, and China.
The industry gives proven reserves a 90% certainty of being produced (P90), probable reserves 50% (P50), and possible reserves 10% (P10).
An integrated oil company is involved in two or more stages of oil production, and high capital costs make barriers to entry very high for new competitors.
Drilling companies generally charge E&P companies for their services based on the amount of time they work.
